observations: The exact goods camera reveals the real slatted deck top, coral rail depth, honey-wood legs and shaped feet as a coherent supported three-quarter object. It clearly reads as the approved conveyor rather than a flat world sprite. The original accepted goods image has noticeably darker legs and flatter rail faces.

The refined native rail shoulders and soft slate slat bands carry through without an added contrast or color grade. Beveled warm wood, restrained vertical grain and small brass joinery improve material readability. There are no blown highlights, near-black support dead spots, muddy overlaps or unintended missing surfaces.

The native 384 image and enlarged view are clean on cream, light, gray and dark backgrounds. The intentionally open functional rail ends match the locked approved geometry; they do not justify adding presentation-only caps. Native coverage is unmodified binary alpha, with ordinary current linear filtering supplying reduced-size edge coverage.

At full-canvas 66 and 96 pixel use, the cool deck stays distinct from the warm rails and supports. Small grain and fasteners simplify naturally without distracting sparkle or a fringe. The card-scale silhouette remains recognizable with comfortable margins.

The actual current cream-card consumer shows the candidate cleanly at 540x960 and 786x1398 portrait sizes and at 1280x720 landscape. Belt and 6 left remain legible, other goods and controls retain their exact appearance, and the icon does not intrude into the label/count area. The landscape icon is smaller, at a 49.5 pixel full-canvas destination, and remains readable.

The context proof is a disposable preview using the actual unmodified EditorPresentation, UISkin, ArtBook and Typography code/assets with a six-item fixture on a solid room placeholder. It proves the current card behavior and does not claim completed full-game world/art integration.
remainingDifferences: The fixed ImageGen target is a single registered world-style view, not a three-quarter modeling blueprint. This supplemental view correctly retains the exact approved native construction and material treatment rather than adding its glossy gold terminal collars or changing proportions.
The native 384 capture has the approved deterministic surface coverage; the reduced previews use the actual current linear filter. No raster smoothing or per-background correction was added.
World placement and final combined goods-atlas cutover are not shown by the placeholder-room context and remain coordinator integration work.
